content.jointProblem: Can a site-specific, benign-trained anomaly detector for Modbus TCP and BACnet/IP flag behavioural drift in ArmaturaSec's unlabelled client traffic at a false-positive rate plant operators tolerate, while producing explanations a plant manager can understand and running on ProtoSense hardware? The first study would test whether the researcher's Modbus autoencoder transfers from its synthetic PLC testbed to real multi-site captures and to BACnet/IP.

rationale.text: Đukić has published an unsupervised anomaly-detection framework specifically for Modbus traffic.

sources.quote: This paper presents an unsupervised anomaly detection framework specifically designed for Modbus traffic analysis.

rationale.text: His Modbus framework operates without labelled attack data by scoring reconstruction error against learned normal patterns.

sources.quote: Anomalies are identified by measuring reconstruction error against learned normal patterns, without requiring labelled attack data.

rationale.text: He has threat-modelling experience for smart-building controllers, which is adjacent to ArmaturaSec's BACnet/IP building-automation context.

sources.quote: This paper applies a structured threat modelling methodology—adapted from STRIDE and augmented with ICS-specific threat categories—to a representative smart building controller architecture.

rationale.text: He has compared SCADA intrusion-detection architectures and highlighted hybrid rules-plus-neural scoring as the best overall balance.

sources.quote: hybrid architectures combining specification-based rules with neural anomaly scoring achieve the best overall balance

rationale.text: He has investigated lightweight recurrent models for on-device intrusion detection on constrained IoT devices.

sources.quote: truncated LSTM and GRU variants—on devices with fewer than 256 KB of RAM.

rationale.text: His University of Novi Sad team contributes ICS intrusion-detection algorithm design, threat modelling and evaluation methodology to the SECURE-ICS monitoring project.

sources.quote: As academic partner, the University of Novi Sad team led by Professor Đukić contributes expertise in intrusion detection algorithm design, threat modelling for ICS environments, and evaluation methodology.

rationale.text: He is open to joint research projects with technology companies.

sources.quote: He is open to supervising industrial PhD students and engaging in joint research projects with technology companies seeking expertise in operational technology security and advanced threat analysis.

constraints.text: The method must work without labelled attack examples; the company has zero examples of malicious traffic.

sources.quote: we have zero examples of malicious traffic and supervised classifiers are useless to us.

constraints.text: The detector must learn a site-specific normal baseline and flag behavioural drift from it.

sources.quote: learns what normal looks like on a specific site and raises a flag when behaviour drifts from that baseline.

constraints.text: Alerts must be explainable to a plant manager in plain language.

sources.quote: we can explain to a plant manager in plain language.

constraints.text: Inference must run on-device without affecting packet forwarding latency; the planned fifth hardware variant is intended to carry a dedicated security processor.

sources.quote: dedicated security processor to support on-device anomaly detection without affecting packet forwarding latency.

constraints.text: The collaboration must use client traffic archives, the hardware bench and firmware codebase under NDA, with one to two company engineers part-time.

sources.quote: We can dedicate one to two engineers part-time to a collaborative project, with access to our traffic archives, our hardware bench, and our existing firmware codebase under NDA.

constraints.text: The joint work must be scheduled around SECURE-ICS, which runs 2023-2025.

sources.quote: The project runs from 2023 to 2025 under the Innovation Fund programme.

risks: >Transfer gap: the Modbus autoencoder evidence is from a synthetic PLC testbed, not from ArmaturaSec's real multi-site captures.
No direct BACnet/IP anomaly-detection evidence is present; the building-automation publication is threat modelling, not BACnet traffic detection.
False positives were severe enough in a previous supervised deployment that clients switched alerts off; the no-label drift detector may still be unacceptable in real plant operations.
On-device evidence is for microcontroller-class IoT devices, not ArmaturaSec's planned security processor or ProtoSense forwarding path; memory and latency need bench testing.
Researcher availability is unknown, and SECURE-ICS runs to 2025, so scheduling capacity may be limited.
Client captures are under NDA, so data access, training location and evaluation protocol may delay work.
questions: Can Professor Đukić confirm his availability and capacity for a joint project, and how would it fit with SECURE-ICS?
What volume, site diversity and protocol-version coverage exist for BACnet/IP and Modbus captures in the archives?
What explanation format do plant managers and ProtoSense operators need, and who validates that explanations are understandable?
What compute, memory and latency budget applies to ProtoSense and the planned fifth hardware variant?
What NDA-compliant data-sharing and evaluation protocol will allow use of client captures without moving raw data off-site?
What no-label evaluation protocol is acceptable: bench red-team injections, held-out public attack traffic, expert review, or a combination?
How should per-site normal behaviour and drift thresholds be defined and updated over time?
